name: calm dark worn asphalt road with sparse aggregate, long hairline cracks, a repair patch and an oil stain, its unconnected edges crumbling into dirt with a darker broken lip and loose chunks, laid as a road network with crossroads and dead ends
label: wasteland_ruins/asphalt

surfaces.part: asphalt road network pieces (crossroads, dead ends, T-junction, square patch) on dirt ground

answer.evidence: This is a flat top-down terrain tileset sheet, 256 px wide at every row from 0 to 191. It has dark asphalt road shapes on a brown dirt field. The roads show cracks, a patch and an oil stain. Their edges crumble into dirt. The column scan shows only alternating dirt and asphalt texture bands with no front-edge line, eave shadow or vertical south face. There is no front face, so the sheet is a plain top-down ground plane, which is normal for terrain.

styleAnswer.evidence: The asphalt reads as a flat slate-blue with only about 3 close steps: a mid tone, a slightly lighter mottling and a darker speckle. The only 'cracks' are a few tiny zigzag marks in the patch on the right, and I can't find long hairline cracks, an oil stain or a distinct repair patch. The dirt is a decent brown mottle with 3-4 tones. The asphalt edges are ragged, but I see no clearly darker broken lip or loose chunks, so the crumbling-edge brief is only weakly met. Measured facts show 5 visible tones per tile against 7 for paving and 3 for grass, with 5% near-flat coverage, which is acceptable. Raw colours total only 12 across the whole piece against 80 for the grass reference, so the piece is thin in shading depth. Dark edge pixels are 0% neutral, so there is no sticker outline, but the material-tone edge treatment is minimal. The result is a repetitive two-material noise pattern that looks flatter and less crafted than the Beodeul references.

surfaces.part: asphalt road network tiles (crossroads, dead ends, T-junctions, a large road slab) on a dirt ground

answer.evidence: The sheet is a fully opaque 256x192 field of flat ground. Dark asphalt road pieces sit on brown dirt, drawn straight down from above. Their crumbling edges are drawn as flat texture. The column scan shows only alternating texture bands (dirt L~105, asphalt-edge L~81, with sparse cracks and aggregate), and none of them forms a front-edge line, eave shadow or vertical face. There is no south face and no receding side face, so it is a flat terrain tile set. This is acceptable for the terrain kind but has no front face by construction.

styleAnswer.evidence: The asphalt is only about 3 steps: a mid blue-grey, a darker and a lighter speckle. The dirt is about 3 browns. The measured 5 visible tones per tile is below the paving reference (7) but above grass (3). Near-flat coverage is 5%, so the large areas carry mottling and are not flat fills. The dark edge pixels are tinted (0% neutral), so there is no black sticker outline, but there is also no distinct darker broken lip, so the outline is none. The asked-for features are weak or missing: the hairline cracks, the oil stain and the loose chunks barely read, and the repair patch is just a faint triangle mark in the large block. The road shapes are blocky and the edges are only slightly ragged. Only 12 colours in total with 3-step ramps is shallower than the 5-6 steps Beodeul uses per material. The surface also looks like uniform noise rather than hand-placed per-stone shading.

surfaces.part: asphalt road tiles and dirt ground, flat top-down autotile sheet

answer.evidence: The sheet is a full-bleed 256px-wide field of dirt with grey-blue asphalt road pieces (T-junctions, crossroads, corners, dead ends, a large block, a small square, a tiny patch). All of it is viewed straight from above. The silhouette is 256 wide on every row, so there is no outline. The column scan shows only texture bands that repeat every 64 rows, with no front-edge line, eave shadow, ellipse or vertical face. No south face of 3 or more rows exists anywhere and no side face is drawn. The crumbling edges are drawn flat as irregular dark lips, not as a raised front face. It reads as a flat top-down ground texture, which fits the terrain kind.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate has only 12 distinct colours in total and about 5 visible tones per tile, against 3 for the grass reference and 7 for the paving reference. The asphalt ramp reads as roughly 3 steps (a dark slate base, a mid tone and a lighter speckle), while Beodeul materials use about 5-6. Its dirt is a similar 3-4 step brown mottle. Near-flat coverage is 5%, so there are no big flat fills, and the speckle gives some grain. The dark edge pixels are 0% neutral, so there is no black sticker outline. But the road edges are mostly a plain value change, and I can't see the darker broken lip, loose chunks or crumbling the brief asks for. The cracks, repair patch and oil stain are tiny and weak; the repair patch has only a few small marks and the cracks are barely there. The surface is a repeated noise pattern, with none of the per-stone shading or clump variety of the references. The dead ends and crossroads do read as a network, but the asphalt is shallower and sparser than the paving reference, so it would look thinner beside it. When in doubt, fail.

surfaces.part: asphalt road network (straight, crossroad, corner, T-junction and dead-end pieces, plus a large filled slab with a repair patch) on a dirt ground

answer.evidence: This is a flat terrain tileset seen straight down: dark asphalt road pieces on brown dirt, filling all 192 rows. The column scan shows only alternating texture bands (dirt, asphalt, crack and stain rows). There is no front-edge line, eave shadow, vertical south face, ellipse or receding side face. The road edges crumble into dirt in plan view only. No standing volume is drawn, so there is no front face of 3 or more rows. As a ground tile, the whole image is the top surface.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate has only 12 distinct colours in total and 5 visible tones per tile, against 7 for the paving reference. The asphalt is a mottled blue-grey with about 3 lightness steps (dark, mid, light speckle), which is shallow next to the paving reference's 5-6. The dirt is brown with scattered darker and lighter dots, which gives some grain, but the asphalt has no visible hairline cracks, repair patch or oil stain, so the main material detail is thin. The crumbling edge is a dark lip with little breakup and no loose chunks to speak of. Edge pixels are tinted rather than neutral black (0% neutral), and no sticker outline is visible. Near-flat coverage is 5%, low but above both references' 0%. Overall it is a mid-level, simplified rendering that falls below the Beodeul reference on ramp depth and surface detail.
